clue.text: Mum meeting someone in Glasgow? It's supposed to be lucky

parts.note: mum is a mother, informally MA
a person in Glasgow is likely a Scot

explanation.surface: A mother meets a Glaswegian, and something about it is meant to bring good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A team's charm figure or animal is kept because it is believed to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Lively soldier drowning in booze

indicators.note: drowning in means the soldier is submerged within the drink

parts.note: ale is beer, booze
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A lively soldier is awash with drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Agile means nimble and quick-moving, close in sense to lively.

clue.text: Business groups getting on, type retained by American agency

indicators.note: retained by means the agency holds these words inside it

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
taken as written
a type is a sort or kind

explanation.surface: Corporate partnerships getting along under the eye of US intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia are associations of companies pooling resources for a venture.

clue.text: Islander in trouble not turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to nag is to trouble or pester

explanation.surface: An islander is in difficulty for failing to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses NAG + NOT, giving the letters bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Pacific island kingdom, so a native of it is an islander.

clue.text: 'Goody' about to catch 'baddy' — they run at a moderate pace

definitions.text: they run at a moderate pace

indicators.note: to catch means the reversed letters close around the villain
about means the saint's abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: a goody is a good person, a saint, abbreviated ST
a rotter is a cad or villain

explanation.surface: A melodrama where the hero closes in on the villain.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'Goody' and 'baddy' look like characters in a story; 'about' gives TS and 'to catch' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses that trot move at a gait between walking and cantering, so they are trotters.

clue.text: Scruffy kids, a lot I smartened somehow after short time

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Ragged children are tidied up after a brief while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges A LOT I SMARTENED to ATTERDEMALIONS, which goes 'after' T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatterdemalions are people in ragged clothing, ragamuffins, here scruffy youngsters.

clue.text: On the subject of business, the writer is lost for words

parts.note: over can mean about, as in a dispute over money
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
the writer refers to the setter, me

explanation.surface: An author speechless about a business matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overwhelmed by emotion is speechless, unable to find anything to say.

clue.text: Cheers when a politician enters US city

indicators.note: enters means the politician goes in between the thanks word and a

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A toast as a politician arrives in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the west coast of Florida.

clue.text: Vibrancy of English boy in foreign country, blasting off loudly

indicators.note: in means the English boy sits within the country
blasting off suggests the letter for loudly is shot away from the country

parts.note: France is a foreign country from a British viewpoint
f, forte, is the musical marking for loudly
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An English lad abroad loses his voice from shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasting off' leaves RANCE, the musical forte sign gone; 'in' makes the container. 'Loudly' reads as describing the blasting but is the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Resonance is a deep, ringing richness of sound, the quality of vibrancy.

clue.text: Tinge Monet conjured up for herbaceous plant

indicators.note: conjured up suggests magicking these letters into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Monet magically produces a tint that becomes a painted flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignonette is a fragrant garden plant of the reseda family, grown as a herbaceous annual.

clue.text: Japanese ingredient is included by Maureen

indicators.note: included by means the word is goes inside the name's short form

parts.note: Mo is a common short form of the name Maureen

explanation.surface: Maureen's recipe calls for a Japanese ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is a fermented soybean paste used widely in Japanese cooking.

clue.text: Embellish talk to be given at end of month

indicators.text: to be given at end of
indicators.note: to be given at end of places the speech word after the month

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
to orate is to talk formally, to make a speech

explanation.surface: Someone is told to dress up a speech due at the month's end.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish something is to adorn or ornament it, which is what decorating does.

clue.text: Knowing about bar's closing and opening

indicators.note: about means the shrewd word goes round the letter picked

parts.note: canny means shrewd or knowing

indicators.note: closing points to the final letter of bar's

explanation.surface: A shrewd remark about when the pub shuts and opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' sits at the end looking like part of the pub-hours picture, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a small gap or chink, a narrow opening in a wall or rock.

clue.text: Member of tribe about to get instruction in English language

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
ELT stands for English Language Teaching

explanation.surface: A tribesman is about to be given English lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: The Celts were an ancient group of peoples, so one of them belongs to a tribe.

clue.text: To kill time, I acted strangely

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: strangely means the letters behave oddly and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone passing time by acting oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or destroy completely, as when killing pests.

clue.text: What's having detrimental effect on mother, getting old?

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially livestock
aging means growing old

explanation.surface: A question about what harms a mother as she grows older.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmful has a damaging effect; the two describe the same injurious quality.

clue.text: Fighter, happy one attending common soldiers

parts.note: glad means happy
I is the Roman numeral one
at means present at, attending
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A cheerful fighter mixing with the rank and file.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a Roman combatant who fought in the arena.

clue.text: Terrible performer? Not a person taking charge

parts.note: dire means terrible

indicators.note: not means the a is dropped from the performer word

parts.note: an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A bad actor is told he is no leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A director is the person who runs and oversees something, such as a film or company.

clue.text: Pig a man's destroyed in one form of religion

indicators.note: destroyed means these letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A man's pig is destroyed as part of a religious rite.
explanation.definitionFit: Paganism is a polytheistic or nature-worshipping belief system, a kind of religion.

clue.text: Help with a risky venture

parts.note: a bet is a gamble, a risky venture

explanation.surface: Someone offers assistance with a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: US chum needs to obtain sum of money allocated

parts.note: bud, short for buddy, is American slang for a friend
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: An American friend has to raise some funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget is an amount of money set aside for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Major digital operator at ground level?

definitions.text: Major digital operator at ground level?

parts.words: Major digital operator at ground level?
parts.note: major means big and a digit can be a toe as well as a finger; the largest digit of the foot works at floor level

explanation.surface: Sounds like a big tech company working on the ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest digit on the human foot is the biggest toe, which meets the ground.

clue.text: Add more liquid to pot, we deduce!

parts.note: in a down entry the letters of the clue's pot read upwards spell the first word, so the answer as wordplay describes pot going up

explanation.surface: Someone works out that the pot needs refilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: the first word written upwards in a down light gives the clue's pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish a container is to fill it again with liquid up to the brim.

clue.text: Worst group for tackling tricky issue

indicators.note: tackling means the group word takes hold of the jumbled letters

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of issue are twisted

explanation.surface: The worst team is the one taking on a difficult problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' gives USIES and 'tackling' is the container; 'tackling' reads as sporting, the group as a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Lousiest is a slang superlative for the very poorest in quality.

clue.text: Old novelist in shed in the home counties

indicators.note: in means the shed word is placed within the region's abbreviation

parts.note: SE, south-east, is the region of England containing the home counties
a hut is a shed

explanation.surface: A former writer lives in a garden shed near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are the counties around London, in England's south-east. Nevil Shute wrote A Town Like Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevil Shute was a twentieth-century British-Australian writer of popular fiction.

clue.text: Instrument used by Charpentier

indicators.note: used by suggests the composer's name contains these letters within it

explanation.surface: The French composer Charpentier wrote for a particular instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A harp is a large stringed instrument plucked with the fingers.

clue.text: Well planned, albeit needing someone to promote business

parts.note: albeit means although, or though
a tout solicits custom, drumming up business

explanation.surface: A business plan is sound, though it needs a salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carefully considered in advance is well planned.

clue.text: Places like Plymouth, Southampton, each involved in games

indicators.note: involved in means the abbreviation is set within the games word

parts.note: sports are games

explanation.surface: English coastal towns each take part in sporting contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Plymouth and Southampton are English harbour towns on the south coast, examples of the category.

clue.text: Country fare for major festival

definitions.meaning: a nation straddling Europe and Asia, capital Ankara
the bird traditionally eaten at Christmas or Thanksgiving

explanation.surface: Food from the countryside served at a big celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the Anatolian nation and the roast bird eaten at Christmas.
